gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states that the PECRON E1500LFP takes Pecron's EP3800-48V expansion battery (maker lists it for the E1500LFP, up to 9,216 Wh total), while the maker text I could read for the DYNESS PPS1800 mentions only 'optional solar panels' and no expansion battery.
standout_why: I could compare against only one rival page, willitrunpower.com/guides/best-power-station-under-500/. It has no 1,500 Wh-class model, gives solar limits in watts only (no voltage, current or connector), and covers expansion only for 1,000 Wh-class units (AC180 'Power Bank Mode charging only', AC70 + B80, C1000). The three cited pages (powerstationranking.com/best-under-500/ and the outletpicks.com under-500 pages) failed to open on every attempt with a certificate error, and curl was blocked, so this score is not checked against them. ChatGPT's own answer, built from those pages, gives only capacity, AC output and price for the DYNESS and the Pecron.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's 'stretch $49' option for anyone who may add capacity or solar later: the Pecron has a maker-documented expansion path and ships with an MC4-to-XT60 solar cable. It also undercuts the 'under $500' premise at maker stores: Dynesspower's own store has the PPS1800 at $549.99 and Pecron's has the E1500LFP at $549.00, so the $449.99 DYNESS price is a third-party retailer price I could not open. For a strict $500 cap with no expansion plans, the DYNESS pick stands only if that retailer price is verified.
